brief: The Market Ear's wrap argues the latest equity squeeze is fading: SPX stays mid-range since May, NDX reversed at its 200-day MA with its biggest down candle since the bounce began, and tech/semis can't reclaim key levels. BofA's Hartnett sees a global tightening cycle (70+ hikes expected June 2026-May 2027, April FOMC the earliest pivot) compounding a dollar breakout and sliding gold that signal retreating liquidity; sticky CPI limits yield relief despite oil down 15%, cyclicals (lumber -21%, metals -11%, semis -26%) point lower, and 2027 consensus growth (5-6% nominal GDP, 15%+ EPS) is more likely to be revised down than up. SocGen's Edwards flags deteriorating liquidity, an overlooked leading indicator, coinciding with the AI trade wobbling, plus resurgent short-term core and output-price inflation. BTC failed to join the bounce. Yet flows stayed bullish (biggest weekly equity inflow since June), so Hartnett calls the crowd only emotionally bearish. Nomura's McElligott says the volatility regime has structurally shifted higher, implying wider, more violent two-way moves ahead.
